title: It'll never return...
description:
90s nostalgia hits different, and it isn't just because we got older. We were the last generation to grow up before the internet took over everything: an analog childhood, then the world changed underneath us.

Psychologists call it the reminiscence bump: you remember ages 10 to 30 more vividly than any other part of your life. Everybody has one. What's different is what was happening during ours. In this video I break down the five reasons: everything was scarce, there was real mystery, we all watched the same things at the same time, we owned physical things, and we're the bridge generation that saw the world before and after.

00:00 Why 90s nostalgia hits different
00:50 What nostalgia actually is
01:17 1. Everything was scarce
02:23 2. There was mystery
03:26 3. We all watched the same thing
04:10 4. We owned physical things
04:46 5. The bridge generation
05:42 Gen Z is nostalgic too
06:16 It's never coming back

title: You're Not Paying What AI Actually Costs
description:
AI pricing doesn't match what AI costs to run. Your monthly fee is flat, but every prompt costs the company real computing power, and the gap is being covered by investors.

Over the weekend Elon Musk said the cost of serving Grok Bot was "unsustainably high relative to revenue," two weeks after calling it the fastest-growing product he'd ever seen. That isn't just an xAI problem. In this video I break down how flat-rate AI plans actually work, why AI agents broke the buffet model, how few people pay at all, who is covering the losses, and the quiet changes already happening: weekly caps, lighter default models, shared usage pools and token meters.

If you've built your workflow, your business or your content around these tools, plan for a correction. Today's price is not the real price.

00:00 Musk on Grok Bot's costs
01:13 How AI pricing actually works
01:29 The all-you-can-eat buffet problem
01:49 Why AI agents break flat-rate plans
02:05 Anthropic's weekly usage limits
02:26 Most AI users pay nothing
02:46 Who is covering the losses
03:28 Same price, less for your money
04:11 Flat-rate plans are becoming meters
04:24 The counterpoint: older models get cheaper
05:01 Plan for the correction
